sections.h2: What an Illinois quitclaim deed transfers
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed in Illinois hands the grantee whatever interest the grantor holds on the day of signing, and nothing more. Under 765 ILCS 5/10, a deed in the statutory form is a good conveyance, release and quit claim of "all the then existing legal or equitable rights of the grantor" in the described premises. Title the grantor picks up afterward stays behind unless the deed adds words expressing that intention.

That limit explains where the form gets used. It suits transfers between people who already know the ownership history, such as co-owners or relatives. A buyer from the open market gets only what the seller owns, and the statutory form carries no promise about the quality of the title.

The form names the grantor and the consideration, then says the grantor will "convey and quit claim" to the grantee "all interest" in the described real estate in a named county, followed by a date and signature. Party names should be typed or printed under the signatures, and the page should leave a blank space of 3 1/2 inches by 3 1/2 inches for the recorder. Skipping either detail doesn't affect the validity of the deed.

A deed drawn on this pattern normally carries these items:

  • The grantor's name and place of residence
  • The grantee's name or names
  • The consideration stated in the deed
  • The property's legal description plus the Illinois county where it sits
  • The date and the grantor's signature

sections.h2: Filing a deed at the recorder's office
sections.html:
A transfer declaration has to go in with the deed. Section 31-25 of the Property Tax Code requires it to be presented with the deed, or within 3 business days after the transfer takes effect, whichever is earlier. One seller and one buyer, or their attorneys or agents, must sign. Apart from deeds covered by section 31-45, a recorder turns away any deed that arrives alone.

The form asks for the stated value, the parcel number, the legal description, the type of deed, the address, whether the parties are related and any homestead exemptions shown on the latest tax bill. Form PTAX-203 can be completed in MyDec when the county participates, and other counties use fill-in forms. Once the deed is recorded, section 31-30 sends the declaration to the assessor's office, which is how the sale price reaches the county.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a quitclaim deed
sections.html:
The state charges fifty cents for each $500 of the value written on the declaration, and a leftover fraction of a block is counted as a whole one (35 ILCS 200/31-10). Where the document says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the unpaid balance of that mortgage is taken out of the taxable base. Nobody escapes the tax by skipping the recording.

Local charges may be added. The Cook County Clerk posts the two rates below and offers a lookup for each municipality in Cook. Elsewhere, phone the county recorder and ask what else applies.

Section 31-45 lists the exempt deeds and trust documents. Several come up with quitclaims:

  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100
  • Deeds that confirm, correct, modify or supplement a deed already recorded, with no additional consideration
  • Deeds of partition
  • Deeds issued to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in a transfer in lieu of foreclosure
  • Tax deeds
  • Deeds that release property held as security for a debt

Exempt doesn't always mean excused from paperwork. For some categories, including actual exchanges of real estate, the deed is still not exempt from filing the declaration.

sections.h2: What Cook County charges to record a deed
sections.html:
In Cook County a deed falls under Document Class 1 and costs $107 to record. The pieces are a $55 county recording fee, a $23 GIS fee, a $10 document storage fee, an $18 State Rental Housing Support Fee and a $1 non-government filer fee. A filer who isn't subject to the state fee pays $19 less, and mail recording with return adds $5 per document.

Public Act 104-40, effective January 1, 2026, adds a fee exemption to section 10. A quitclaim recorded only to reflect a legal name change, with the same individual or group on both sides, pays no recording fees. Other Illinois counties set their own fee schedules, so ask the county recorder before mailing a deed.

sections.h2: Where the transfer declaration goes after recording
sections.html:
The recorder never records the declaration itself (section 31-30). The deed's document number is written on it, and a copy travels to the county assessor or supervisor of assessments within 30 days of receipt. That office adds the latest assessed value for each parcel, then forwards the batch to the state revenue agency by a deadline tied either to receipt or to the close of the prior year's appeal session, whichever is later.

The assessor may keep a copy to help set the proper valuation of the transferred property and of other parcels in the county. So a quitclaim between relatives for a stated price of a few dollars still leaves a record at the assessor's office, and the figures on the declaration should match the deed.

sections.h2: Using a quitclaim when you want to sell
sections.html:
A quitclaim can carry a sale as long as the signer truly owns the interest being sold, because that is all the buyer gets. Check with the title company handling your closing about which deed form it accepts.

Bring these to the recorder:

  • The signed and dated deed with the blank space reserved for the recorder
  • The completed transfer declaration, signed by a seller and a buyer or their agents
  • The transfer tax, where the transfer is not exempt
  • The county recording fee

If you are selling an inherited or co-owned house as it stands, bring up the deed question with the buyer's side early so the paperwork is done well before closing day.

The work usually runs in this order. Confirm who is on title and what each person holds. Settle the deed form with the title company. Sign the deed and the declaration. Pay any transfer tax and the recording fee when the papers go in. Once the deed is recorded, the declaration moves on to the assessor and the sale price becomes part of the county's file. A cash buyer usually skips the lender's document checklist, so the deed and declaration are often the main items left on the list.

faqs.q: How does an Illinois quitclaim differ from a warranty deed?
faqs.a: A quitclaim conveys only the grantor's then existing legal or equitable rights. It doesn't reach title acquired later unless the deed adds words saying so, and the statutory form carries no promise about the quality of title.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on an Illinois quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: In Cook County the seller is the party liable for both the state and the county tax. Outside Cook, contact the county recorder to learn who is liable and whether a local tax applies.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax owed if the deed is never recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 31-10 makes the tax due whether or not a document is recorded, and it reaches transfers made through one or several related transactions.

faqs.q: Can I record a quitclaim deed just to change the name on my title?
faqs.a: Yes. The recording carries no recording fees when the sole purpose is to reflect a legal name change and the grantor is also the grantee under a new name. The exemption comes from Public Act 104-40, effective January 1, 2026.

faqs.q: How soon must the transfer declaration be filed?
faqs.a: With the deed, or within 3 business days after the transfer takes effect, whichever is earlier. It needs a signature from at least one seller and one buyer, or their attorneys or agents.
